To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of 40 and 60 mmol/l NaCl to a rehydration drink reduces subsequent urine output, but does not improve exercise capacity 4 h after rehydration.
the addition of sodium to a rehydration solution reduced urine output, but did not improve exercise capacity after exercise in the heat.

rehydrating with drinks containing 40 or 40 mmol/l sodium chloride resulted in less urine production than a drink without sodium chloride, but this did not improve exercise capacity 4 h after rehydration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of sodium chloride concentration in a rehydration drink on the rehydration of subjects after moderate hypohydration.
the effect of sodium on the rehydration of the body.
the effects of sodium chloride on rehydration following exercise-induced hypohydratation in man.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a sodium chloride content of 40 mmol/l in a rehydration beverage is optimal for rehydration after exercise-induced hypohyrdration, but does not enhance exercise capacity 4 h after rehydration.
a sodium concentration in the range of 31-50 mmol l-1 in a rehydration drink after exercise-induced hypohydrations of up to about 3% body weight, will not improve subsequent exercise performance.
the addition of 40 mmol sodium to a rehydration drink is more effective than a sodium-free beverage in rehydration, but does not improve subsequent exercise capacity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the addition of sodium chloride to drinks is effective for rehydration after exercise, but the effect is not immediate and may not be apparent in performance until 4 h or longer after the end of exercise.
the addition of 40 mmol/l sodium chloride to a carbohydrate-electrolyte drink improves the rehydration response, but does not improve subsequent exercise performance.
the ingestion of a rehydration solution with sodium content between 31 and 50 meq/L is effective at reducing the amount of urine output, thereby promoting rehydration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a sodium-free beverage is not the best option for rehydration.
the addition of sodium chloride to rehydration beverages is a useful strategy to enhance the rehydration process.
sodium is an important component of a rehydration beverage and that sodium chloride concentration of 40–50 mmol/L is sufficient to enhance rehydration.
